newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday November 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday November 6.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Leftist PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema wrote a supporting letter to former magistrate and Public Works minister Antonio Di Pietro, who has been under fire in recent weeks (all).

* A report from finance police's special branch Gico is said to affirm that Di Pietro favoured banker Francesco Pacini Battaglia, who is currently in jail on charges of corruption, in a previous inquiry (La Repubblica) .
* Ten more people, including magistrates and policemen, were put under preliminary investigation in La Spezia in a corruption probe (all).

* In the first day of voting over the 1997 draft budget in the Lower House the tension was high between majority party and opposition: some opposition Freedom Alliance deputies left the Chamber for an hour so that the house was not quorate (all).

* In a report from Brussels, the European Commission is said to expect all European countries except Italy and Greece to meet budget deficit targets for the single currency. Forecasts for Italy's 1997 deficit are at 3.3 percent of GDP, but the Treasury is optimistic (all).
* Italian bond futures hit new highs at 125.80 in wave of buying on EMU hopes (all).
* Cerus, a holding owned by Carlo De Benedetti, announced it was selling its 27.4 per cent stake in French car parts maker Valeo to CGIP and others, expecting gains for 1.95 trillion lire (all).
* Enzo Berlanda, chairman of stock exchange watchdog Consob, says he is "not convinced" by the government rescue plan for ailing Banco di Napoli (Sole 24 Ore).

* The Upper House Public Works commission will resume today discussions to try to break the stalemate over a law decree on telecommunications sector watchdog, which is a prerequisite for the privatisation of telecom holding Stet (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
